study: Clarke et al. 2015 (Early Learning in Mathematics [ELM] K core curriculum + teacher PD)
eval_evidence: Study authored by the program developers under IES Award R305A080699; 'In Oregon, the lead author of ELM provided the trainings. In Texas, the lead author led trainings' — the ELM developers conducted the efficacy evaluation.
developer_evidence: The lead author of ELM (developer/research team) provided/led the teacher trainings in both states.
cascade_evidence: Lead author (developer) delivered the trainings directly to the kindergarten teachers; no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Control classrooms 'taught mathematics as they would typically' / adhered to standard district mathematics instruction (business-as-usual); they received a stipend only.
coaching_evidence: PD = an initial 2-4h logistics meeting plus three 4-hour ELM curriculum workshop trainings (fall/winter/spring). Classroom visits by project staff were fidelity observations (COSTI-M), not ongoing in-class instructional coaching.
student_dose_evidence: ELM is a Tier-1 whole-class core kindergarten math curriculum taught by the regular teacher during normal math time; no pull-out, tutoring, or extra student dose.
maturity_evidence: Single kindergarten implementation year per cohort (Oregon 2008-09, Texas 2009-10); teachers were new to ELM and outcomes measured at end of that first implementation year (the grade-1 SAT-10 is a follow-up of the same first-year cohort).
